title: Colonoscopy: Pre-Procedure Assessment and Bowel Preparation

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult booked for an elective colonoscopy in a Saudi hospital or endoscopy unit: indication and screening pathway, safety assessment (kidney, heart, diabetes, blood thinners, pregnancy, obstruction), choice of bowel preparation, diet, split-dose timing, instructions to the patient, on-the-day check of cleanliness and what to do when the preparation is poor. Uses the European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy bowel preparation guideline, the British Society of Gastroenterology and ESGE antithrombotic guideline, the Saudi Ministry of Health colorectal screening page and the product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national guideline on bowel preparation for colonoscopy was found; the ESGE 2019 guideline is a European guideline and was read through a French (SFED) translation of its 17 recommendations because the English journal page was blocked. The full guideline text was not read, only the numbered recommendation statements.

The Saudi Ministry of Health page gives the screening pathway (age 45 to 75, fecal immunochemical test every year for moderate risk, colonoscopy for increased risk or a positive test, repeat every ten years if normal); a review of Saudi screening says there is no formal national programme and that in a Ministry pilot only 20.4% of people with a positive test had a colonoscopy.

Saudi-specific bowel preparation data were not found; a randomised trial from the Royal Hospital in Muscat, Oman (a Gulf neighbour) is used: split-dose 4 L polyethylene glycol gave adequate preparation in 89.2% versus 62.5% with single dose, and hypertension and diabetes predicted inadequate preparation.

The GoLYTELY label gives a 4 litre single-evening regimen; the split-dose version (2 L in the evening, 2 L on the morning of the procedure) follows ESGE and the Oman trial and is not the labelled regimen.

Generic polyethylene glycol 4 litre products sold in Saudi Arabia (for example Nulytely and Klean-Prep) were not checked for composition or sachet size; the US GoLYTELY label is used as a reference for the 4 litre class.
G6PD deficiency is common in the Gulf region; the MoviPrep label cautions about its sodium ascorbate and ascorbic acid in G6PD deficiency, and local prevalence figures were not checked.
Oral simethicone is suggested by ESGE but no label or dose was reviewed, so none is written; sodium phosphate and enemas are not recommended by ESGE.

The thresholds on antithrombotic management are from the 2021 BSG and ESGE guideline and apply to low-risk (diagnostic) and high-risk (polypectomy) colonoscopy; individual cardiology or haematology advice is needed for high thrombotic risk, and no warfarin, heparin or direct oral anticoagulant regimen label was reviewed, so none is written.
Diabetes medicine adjustment on the day of preparation, sedation assessment and pregnancy-specific advice are mentioned but not detailed; no source with a regimen was read.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Good visualisation of the colon needs clean bowel; poor preparation causes missed polyps, longer procedures, incomplete examinations and repeat colonoscopy (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 15). Splitting the preparation so the last dose is taken close to the colonoscopy gives the cleanest right colon and the highest adenoma detection (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6). A low fibre diet the day before reduces residue in the colon (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 1). Osmotic laxatives pull water into the bowel and cause large fluid shifts; the risk of dehydration, low sodium, low potassium or kidney injury is higher in older people and in kidney, heart or liver disease (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.1 and 5.4). Bowel preparation lowers absorption of other medicines taken at the same time, so oral medicines are taken at least an hour before (GoLYTELY label, Drug Interactions 7.2). Polyps grow slowly over 5 to 10 years, so screening colonoscopy can prevent cancer (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section What is colorectal cancer).

symptoms: Bleeding from the back passage or blood in the stool (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Symptoms).
Change in bowel habit, persistent abdominal pain or unexplained weight loss (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Symptoms).
No symptoms but age 45 to 75 with a positive stool immunochemical test (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Screening).
Family history of colorectal cancer or polyps, long-standing inflammatory bowel disease (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Target groups).
physicalSigns: Pallor from iron deficiency anaemia (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Symptoms).
Abdominal distension, tenderness or mass that may suggest obstruction: do not give bowel preparation until obstruction is excluded (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.6).
Dehydration and low blood pressure before preparation (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.1).
Constipation, diabetes, hypertension and previous poor preparation predict inadequate cleaning (Oman split-dose trial, Results).
redFlags: Suspected bowel obstruction, perforation, toxic colitis, toxic megacolon, ileus or gastric retention: do not give bowel preparation (GoLYTELY label, Contraindications 4; MoviPrep label, Contraindications 4).
Severe renal impairment with creatinine clearance below 30 mL per minute: sodium picosulfate with magnesium oxide (Clenpiq) is contraindicated (Clenpiq label, Contraindications 4).

Vomiting, severe abdominal pain or bloating during preparation: stop and delay the next dose until it settles; seek urgent care for persistent symptoms (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.2; GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.1).
Seizure, fainting, palpitations or confusion during or after preparation: check electrolytes urgently (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.1 to 5.3).

Warfarin or direct anticoagulant not stopped before polypectomy, or anticoagulated with high thrombotic risk: plan with cardiology or haematology before the date (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Summary of recommendations).
Rectal bleeding with haemodynamic instability on anticoagulants: urgent hospital care (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Summary of recommendations).
precipitants: Hypertension and diabetes (Oman split-dose trial, Results).
Chronic constipation, previous abdominal surgery, immobility or previous inadequate preparation (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 17).
Single-dose rather than split-dose preparation (Oman split-dose trial, Results; ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6).
Poor understanding of the instructions or language barriers (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 2).
Drugs affecting kidney function or electrolytes: diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers and NSAIDs (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm the indication and the pathway
actions: Screening: age 45 to 75 with no symptoms and a positive fecal immunochemical test, or increased risk (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Target groups).
Diagnostic: bleeding, anaemia, change in bowel habit or weight loss (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Symptoms).
Make sure people with a positive screening test are booked for colonoscopy; in a Ministry pilot only 20.4% went on to have one (Screening review of Saudi Arabia, Section Recent Screening Projects).

clinicalManagement.title: Check safety before preparation
actions: Ask about obstruction symptoms, inflammatory bowel disease, kidney, heart and liver disease, seizures, pregnancy and G6PD status (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.1 to 5.8; MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.8).
Check creatinine and electrolytes in older people and those with risk factors; correct abnormalities (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.1).
Review blood thinners and diabetes medicines and give written instructions (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Summary of recommendations).
Check which medicines affect kidney function or electrolytes (diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, NSAIDs) (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Plan antiplatelet and anticoagulant medicines
actions: Continue aspirin for all colonoscopy; continue P2Y12 antagonists for low-risk (diagnostic) procedures (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Summary of recommendations).

Warfarin: continue for low-risk procedures if the international normalised ratio is in range; stop 5 days before high-risk procedures such as polypectomy in low thrombotic risk and check the ratio is below 1.5 (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Warfarin and heparin).

Direct oral anticoagulants: omit the morning dose for low-risk procedures; for high-risk procedures take the last dose 3 days before (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Summary of recommendations).
For high thrombotic risk liaise with cardiology or haematology; restart up to 2 to 3 days later (BSG and ESGE antithrombotic guideline 2021, Section Summary of recommendations).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose the preparation
actions: Use polyethylene glycol (high or low volume) or a validated non-polyethylene glycol product; individualise in people at risk of fluid and electrolyte disturbance (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 9).
Do not use oral sodium phosphate routinely and do not use enemas routinely (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 5 and Recommendation 10).
In inflammatory bowel disease, urgent bleeding or pregnancy, use a polyethylene glycol preparation (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 12, Recommendation 13 and Recommendation 14).

clinicalManagement.title: Give enhanced instructions
actions: Give written and verbal instructions in the patient's language, with a diet sheet and timings (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 2 and Recommendation 16).
Advise a low fibre diet the day before and clear liquids afterwards (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 1).
Split the preparation so that the last dose starts within 5 hours of the colonoscopy and ends at least 2 hours before (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6 and Recommendation 8).
Take other oral medicines at least 1 hour before starting each dose (MoviPrep label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Check the preparation on the day
actions: Ask about the doses taken, clear stool and symptoms; check pulse, blood pressure and glucose if diabetic (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 16).
If the effluent is not clear, give extra preparation and consider same-day or next-day colonoscopy (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 15).
Score the preparation with a validated scale at the procedure (Oman split-dose trial, Methods).

clinicalManagement.title: Repeat or follow up
actions: Repeat colonoscopy within 1 year if preparation was inadequate, adjusting the next preparation to the cause (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 15).
Set the next screening interval per the Saudi page: ten years if normal in moderate risk (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Screening periodicity).
Monitor adequate-preparation rates for the unit (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 15).

regimens.indication: Cleansing of the colon before colonoscopy
regimens.patientGroup: Adults for elective colonoscopy, including those with kidney, heart or electrolyte risk
regimens.dose: 4 litres of reconstituted solution; the label gives the whole 4 litres in the evening before the colonoscopy; the split regimen recommended by ESGE gives 2 litres in the evening and 2 litres early on the morning of the colonoscopy (Oman split-dose trial, Methods; ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6). Dilution and preparation: add lukewarm drinking water to the 4-litre fill line of the supplied container and shake until dissolved; do not reconstitute with other liquids and do not add starch-based thickeners; keep refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and use within 48 hours (GoLYTELY label, Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2).
regimens.route: Oral; drink 8 ounces (about 240 mL) every 10 minutes until the dose is finished or the rectal effluent is clear; a loose watery stool should start in about an hour; via nasogastric tube 20 to 30 mL per minute if needed (GoLYTELY label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
regimens.frequency: Split into two 2-litre doses: evening before and morning of colonoscopy; start the second dose within 5 hours of the colonoscopy and finish at least 2 hours before it (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 8)
regimens.duration: One day of preparation; clear liquids until 2 hours before the procedure
adjustments: Label is a single 4-litre evening dose; the split regimen follows ESGE and is a departure from the label (GoLYTELY label, Dosage and Administration 2.2; ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6).
Take oral medicines within 1 hour before starting the preparation because it reduces drug absorption (GoLYTELY label, Drug Interactions 7.2).
Renal impairment and drugs that affect kidney function (diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, NSAIDs): use with caution and advise good hydration (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.4).
Heart failure: use caution when replacing fluids (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.1).

Pregnancy: give only if clearly needed (GoLYTELY label, Use in Specific Populations 8.1); ESGE says PEG may be considered if colonoscopy is strongly indicated (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 13).
Pediatric safety and effectiveness have not been established (GoLYTELY label, Use in Specific Populations 8.4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Hydration, vomiting and orthostatic hypotension; consider post-procedure electrolytes, creatinine and urea if significant vomiting (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.1).
Abdominal pain, bloating, nausea; stop and review if severe (GoLYTELY label, Adverse Reactions 6).
Clarity of the last stools before the colonoscopy (GoLYTELY label, Dosage and Administration 2.2).
Signs of anaphylaxis: rash, angioedema, breathing difficulty (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.8).
contraindications: Gastrointestinal obstruction, bowel perforation, toxic colitis or toxic megacolon, gastric retention, ileus (GoLYTELY label, Contraindications 4).
Hypersensitivity to any component (GoLYTELY label, Contraindications 4).
Caution with impaired gag reflex or risk of aspiration; use caution in severe active ulcerative colitis (GoLYTELY label, Warnings 5.6 and 5.7).
regimens.useWhen: Preferred first choice: high-volume polyethylene glycol is safe in kidney, heart and electrolyte risk, in inflammatory bowel disease, pregnancy and bleeding, and split dosing gave 89.2% adequate preparation in a Gulf trial.
regimens.sourceTitle: GoLYTELY (polyethylene glycol 3350 and electrolytes) for oral solution: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6 to Recommendation 9; GoLYTELY US label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2, Section Contraindications 4

regimens.indication: Cleansing of the colon before colonoscopy with a lower-volume polyethylene glycol preparation
regimens.patientGroup: Adults who cannot take 4 litres and have no G6PD deficiency or phenylketonuria
regimens.dose: Two doses, each made from 1 Pouch A and 1 Pouch B in the mixing container filled with water to the fill line (1 litre), then a further 16 ounces (about 500 mL) of clear liquid; Pouch A holds 100 g PEG 3350, 7.5 g sodium sulfate, 2.691 g sodium chloride and 1.015 g potassium chloride; Pouch B holds 4.7 g ascorbic acid and 5.9 g sodium ascorbate (MoviPrep label, Dosage Forms and Strengths and Dosage and Administration 2.2). Dilution and preparation: dissolve completely in water, do not use other liquids or starch-based thickeners; keep the solution upright and refrigerated and use within 24 hours (MoviPrep label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).
regimens.route: Oral; drink 8 ounces (about 240 mL) every 15 minutes, taking about an hour; follow with clear liquid; finish dose 2 at least 2 hours before the colonoscopy (MoviPrep label, Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2)
regimens.frequency: Dose 1 in the evening before; dose 2 about 12 hours after the start of dose 1 and at least 3.5 hours before the colonoscopy (MoviPrep label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
regimens.duration: One day of preparation; the label also describes an evening-only regimen as an alternative when split dosing is inappropriate (MoviPrep label, Dosage and Administration 2.3)
adjustments: Consider G6PD deficiency: use with caution because it contains sodium ascorbate and ascorbic acid, especially with active infection, haemolysis history or oxidant drugs (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.8).
Contains phenylalanine in some flavours; risks in phenylketonuria (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.9).
Do not take oral medicines within 1 hour before or after starting each dose (MoviPrep label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).
Renal impairment, arrhythmia risk and seizure risk: use with caution and correct electrolytes first (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.1 to 5.4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Hydration, vomiting and signs of electrolyte disturbance (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.1).
Palpitations or irregular heartbeat (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.2).
Seizure or loss of consciousness (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.3).
Haemolysis symptoms in G6PD deficiency (MoviPrep label, Warnings 5.8).
contraindications: Gastrointestinal obstruction, bowel perforation, gastric retention, ileus, toxic colitis or toxic megacolon (MoviPrep label, Contraindications 4).
Hypersensitivity to any ingredient (MoviPrep label, Contraindications 4).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when a patient cannot drink 4 litres; avoid in G6PD deficiency and phenylketonuria.
regimens.sourceTitle: MOVIPREP (polyethylene glycol 3350, sodium sulfate, sodium chloride, potassium chloride, ascorbic acid and sodium ascorbate) for oral solution: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 9; MoviPrep US label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 to 2.3, Section Warnings 5.1 to 5.9, Section Contraindications 4

regimens.indication: Cleansing of the colon before colonoscopy with a non-polyethylene glycol preparation
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with creatinine clearance of 30 mL per minute or more who cannot take polyethylene glycol
regimens.genericName: Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide and anhydrous citric acid
regimens.dose: Two doses of one bottle each; each 175 mL bottle contains 10 mg sodium picosulfate, 3.5 g magnesium oxide and 12 g anhydrous citric acid (Clenpiq label, Dosage Forms and Strengths and Dosage and Administration 2.2). Dilution and preparation: ready to drink, do not dilute; store at room temperature and do not refrigerate (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.1 and How Supplied).
regimens.route: Oral; drink the bottle, then at least five 8-ounce cups of clear liquids over the next 5 hours (dose 1) and four or more cups after dose 2, stopping all liquids at least 2 hours before the colonoscopy (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
regimens.frequency: Dose 1 in the evening before (5 to 9 pm); dose 2 the next morning starting about 5 hours before the colonoscopy (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
adjustments: Contraindicated if creatinine clearance is below 30 mL per minute because magnesium accumulates; use with caution in mild to moderate renal impairment (Clenpiq label, Contraindications 4 and Warnings 5.3).
If severe bloating, distension or abdominal pain follows dose 1, delay dose 2 until it settles (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.2).

Take oral medicines at least 1 hour before each dose; tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, iron, digoxin, chlorpromazine and penicillamine at least 2 hours before and not less than 6 hours after (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).
Approved for adults and children 9 years and older; this topic is for adults (Clenpiq label, Indications 1).
Syncope and seizures have been reported; drink balanced electrolyte clear liquids (Clenpiq label, Warnings 5.1, 5.2 and 5.5).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Hydration, electrolytes, syncope and seizures (Clenpiq label, Warnings 5.1 to 5.5).
Severe abdominal pain or bloating after dose 1 (Clenpiq label, Dosage and Administration 2.2).
Creatinine and magnesium in kidney risk (Clenpiq label, Warnings 5.3).
contraindications: Creatinine clearance below 30 mL per minute (Clenpiq label, Contraindications 4).
Gastrointestinal obstruction or ileus, bowel perforation, toxic colitis or toxic megacolon, gastric retention (Clenpiq label, Contraindications 4).
Hypersensitivity to any ingredient (Clenpiq label, Contraindications 4).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when polyethylene glycol is not tolerated and creatinine clearance is 30 mL per minute or higher with no electrolyte disturbance.
regimens.sourceTitle: CLENPIQ (sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide and anhydrous citric acid) oral solution: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 9; Clenpiq US label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2, Section Contraindications 4 and Section Warnings 5

branches.label: Bowel cleansing before colonoscopy
branches.entryCriteria: Adult booked for elective colonoscopy with no bowel obstruction, perforation, ileus, toxic colitis or gastric retention, no allergy to the product, and fluid and electrolyte problems corrected.

medicationPlan.note: Which cleansing agent and when follows the ESGE 2019 guideline; doses, dilution, administration method and contraindications come from the product labels named in each row. The labelled regimens are for adults. Cleansing agents are exclusive alternatives: give one. SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Age 45 to 75 with no symptoms and no family history; yearly fecal immunochemical test (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Target groups and Screening periodicity).
Increased-risk groups or a positive fecal immunochemical test; if normal repeat every ten years in moderate risk (Saudi MOH Colorectal Cancer Awareness page, Section Screening periodicity).
Split-dose for elective colonoscopy; same-day dosing acceptable for afternoon colonoscopy (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 6 and Recommendation 7).
Start within 5 hours of the colonoscopy and finish at least 2 hours before it (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 8).
Low fibre diet on the day before the colonoscopy (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 1).
Repeat colonoscopy within 1 year unless contraindicated; same or next day after extra preparation can be considered (ESGE bowel preparation guideline 2019, Recommendation 15).

teaching.scope: Adult booked for an elective colonoscopy in a Saudi hospital or endoscopy unit: indication and screening pathway, safety assessment (kidney, heart, diabetes, blood thinners, pregnancy, obstruction), choice of bowel preparation, diet, split-dose timing, instructions to the patient, on-the-day check of cleanliness and what to do when the preparation is poor. Uses the European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy bowel preparation guideline, the British Society of Gastroenterology and ESGE antithrombotic guideline, the Saudi Ministry of Health colorectal screening page and the product labels.
learningObjectives: Check indication, kidney function, electrolytes, blood thinners and diabetes before choosing a preparation.
Use a split-dose preparation with a low fibre diet the day before.
Start the last dose within 5 hours and finish at least 2 hours before the colonoscopy.
Give written and verbal instructions and repeat colonoscopy within a year if the preparation is poor.
pitfalls: Single-dose preparation for a morning colonoscopy.
Not checking kidney function in older people.
Forgetting G6PD deficiency with ascorbate products.
Vague instructions given only in English.
Not repeating the colonoscopy after a poor preparation.
keyPoints: Do not give preparation if obstruction, perforation, toxic colitis or ileus is suspected.
Sodium picosulfate with magnesium is contraindicated below 30 mL per minute of creatinine clearance.
Take other oral medicines at least an hour before each dose.
Sodium phosphate and routine enemas are not recommended.

patientEducation: A clean bowel is the most important thing for a good examination.
Eat a low-fibre diet the day before and drink only clear liquids when told.
Take the first dose in the evening and the second dose early the next morning, finishing at least 2 hours before the test.
Take your usual medicines at least an hour before each dose unless you were told otherwise.
Tell us if you vomit, feel faint, have severe stomach pain or cannot finish the drink.
Keep drinking clear fluids to stay hydrated and ask about your blood thinner or diabetes tablets.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid red and purple drinks and seeds or skins the day before.
Arrange transport and a companion if you will have sedation.
Stay close to a toilet during preparation.
Keep barrier cream for the skin around the anus.
Bring a list of your medicines.
mdtReferrals: Gastroenterologist or colorectal surgeon; endoscopy nurse; primary care physician; pharmacist; anaesthetist for sedation; cardiologist or haematologist for anticoagulation; dietitian.
dischargeCriteria: Preparation quality score recorded; findings and biopsies explained; next screening or surveillance interval and repeat plan if the preparation was poor; blood thinners restarted as planned; warning signs of bleeding or perforation given.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Colonoscopy result visit as arranged; repeat within 1 year if inadequate preparation; next screening interval of ten years if normal in moderate risk; surveillance per findings.
